original.text: jīvo uvaogamao amutti kattā sadehaparimāṇo / bhottā saṃsārattho siddho so vissasoḍḍhagaī
original.edition: recalled by the unit author (wording believed standard; to be checked against an edition)

paraphrase: The soul is characterised by cognition, is formless, is the doer, is the size of its body, is the enjoyer, is in worldly existence, is perfected, and naturally moves upward.
notes: Each attribute is said to hold from a particular standpoint (the commentaries). Verse number recalled, not checked; the content is the unit author's recollection (skeleton).

paraphrase: Since the sage attains both kinds of the means of liberation (the ultimate and the conventional) in meditation, practise meditation with an attentive mind.
notes: Verse number recalled, not checked; the content is the unit author's recollection (skeleton).

paraphrase: Recite and meditate on the words of the supreme beings of thirty-five, sixteen, six, five, four, two and one [syllables], and others according to the teacher's instruction.
notes: Commentaries: 35 = the full five-line homage; 16 = 'arhat-siddha-ācārya-upādhyāya-sarvasādhu'; 6 = 'arihanta-siddha'; 5 = 'a-si-ā-u-sā'; 4 = 'arihanta'; 2 = 'siddha'; 1 = 'oṃ' or 'a' (recalled). Verse number recalled, not checked; the content is the unit author's recollection (skeleton).
